items.title: 8.12 The effect of a change of concentration

blocks.text: If a system at equilibrium has some of a reactant or product added or removed, the equilibrium position is disturbed. There are four possibilities. Consider the hydrolysis of bismuth chloride, BiCl3 + H2O giving BiOCl + 2HCl, in which BiCl3 reacts with water to give the white insoluble compound BiOCl; the expression is Kc = [BiOCl][HCl]^2 / ([BiCl3][H2O]). When water is added to a BiCl3 solution it turns cloudy with the white precipitate; at equilibrium some BiOCl and HCl have formed and some BiCl3 remains.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: BiOCl is an insoluble solid and water is the solvent; their concentrations stay constant and are left out of Kc (as the book itself does for solids in its Ksp section). The equilibrium expression is Kc = [HCl]^2 / [BiCl3].

items: Adding BiCl3 or water disturbs the equilibrium; to re-establish it more BiOCl and HCl are produced, the reaction is pushed forward, Kc stays constant but the position changes.
Adding BiOCl or HCl or both: more BiCl3 is produced and the reaction moves in the reverse direction; Kc constant, position changed.
Removing some BiCl3: the reaction moves in the reverse direction to compensate; a new position with Kc constant.
Removing BiOCl or HCl or both: the reaction moves forward to compensate; a new position, Kc constant.
book_errors: Adding BiOCl or HCl or both
Removing BiOCl or HCl or both

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Because BiOCl is a solid, adding or removing some BiOCl does not shift the equilibrium; only adding or removing HCl (or BiCl3) does.
